If a,b,c : R satisfy Reachable a.val c.val and Reachable b.val c.val, but neither Reachable a.val b.val nor Reachable b.val a.val, prove there is no s : R → PathUnfolding.Occurrence root with Function.RightInverse s OccurrencePrefix.reachableEndpoint and ∀ x y : R, Reachable x.val y.val → Reachable (s x) (s y).

Use address = OccurrencePrefix.trace ∘ s. Preservation follows from the assumed source preservation and reachable_iff_prefix. Reflection uses reachable_iff_prefix in reverse, actual PathUnfolding.projection.mapPath, and endpoint identities supplied by RightInverse.

concrete_control.graph_scope: This is the reflexive/transitive thin diamond quiver: identity loops and the bottom→top shortcut are present. It is not the four-edge Hasse DAG. No finite occurrence-set claim is permitted.
proof_obligations: Prove Reachable a b ↔ DiamondLe a b by Path induction with diamondLe_refl/trans and edge.down; the reverse is an actual one-edge path PLift.up h.
Every vertex is reachable from bottom using DiamondLe bottom v. The two middle vertices reach top and cannot reach one another.
Apply the generic obstruction and prove the actual selectedOccurrence section fails reachability preservation. Endpoint right inverse alone remains true.
A positive control must prove the full concrete obstruction. A sole intended negative consumer may then try to pass endpoint_right_inverse as ancestry-preservation evidence.
